evidence.text: CoinShares' own US ETF (BRRR) 10-Q puts bitcoin at $58,391 on 30 June 2026 vs $87,650 on 31 Dec 2025 (-33.4%) and BRRR net assets down 32.3% despite net creations, so group gross AUM of $7.4bn at FY2025 falls to roughly $5bn at 30 June; at the disclosed blended 170bp yield that is ~$50m of H1 asset-management revenue against $126.4m for FY2025, i.e. an annualised run-rate that turns the 3.0x trailing P/E screeners still display on CSHR into roughly 12x.
evidence.why_not_priced: There is no consensus to be surprised against: the only visible sell-side coverage is a single KBW initiation (Outperform, PT cut $9 to $7), and CoinShares has published no interim P&L covering any part of 2026 - the last hard number on the tape is the 1 May 2026 FY2025 release headlined 'Reflecting Continued Strong Growth'. If the earnings-power reset were priced, the stock would not still be carried at a 3.04 P/E and a 7.66% indicated yield on the retail data pages that most of a 202k-ADV de-SPAC's marginal buyers read, and the 20-day run-up would not be +5.0%.
evidence.independence: The FY2025 release itself gives the $7.4bn AUM, $126.4m asset-management revenue and ~170bp blended yield used to convert the AUM decline into revenue: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2087587/000121390026050703/ea028870801ex99-1.htm (6-K, 2026-05-01). evidence.text: Capital Markets - 37% of FY2025 revenue and gains ($73.1m) but 44% of segment EBITDA ($57.7m of $131.3m) - is the one line that cannot be reconstructed from the monthly AUM CoinShares publishes, and its largest single component was disclosed as ETH staking at $4.3m in Q2 2025 alone, a line that scales with token price and with a futures basis that compressed through a half in which industry ETP AUM fell from ~$160bn in May to ~$141bn by 1 June on record outflows.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sweep's own cheap read is that H1 fee revenue is reconstructable from published fund-flow data; that is exactly why the market will anchor on AUM and mis-size the half. A US investor modelling CSHR as an asset manager applies a fee rate to AUM and gets the smaller, more resilient half of segment EBITDA right and the larger, regime-dependent half wrong. If this were understood, the name would not be quoted on a trailing P/E at all and the 63% realised vol would already have an option chain around it rather than 368 total open interest.
evidence.independence: The segment split it rests on comes from the FY2025 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2087587/000121390026050703/ea028870801ex99-1.htm, 2026-05-01), which is shared with finding 1; the Q2 2025 release and the fund-flow volume (https://researchblog.coinshares.com/volume-288-digital-asset-fund-flows-weekly-report-166b82513893, 2026-06-01) are the independent legs.

evidence.why_not_priced: The 1 October lock-up date appears nowhere in the wire copy on the print; it is a clause inside a trading-plan press release, and no earnings preview or calendar row carries it. evidence.independence: The EGM resolutions (25% buyback authority at $0.01-$20.00, 11% pool, 3% evergreen 2027-2029, 131.8m shares outstanding, record date 27 August) are a separate document: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CSHR/notice-of-virtual-extraordinary-general-meeting-of-coin-shares-plc-60dgtz7l5wya.html (2026-08-24), filed as a 6-K at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002087587/000121390026092804/ea0303148-6k_coinshares.htm.

evidence.text: MillerKnoll has submitted refund claims on 'substantially all IEEPA tariffs paid' and had recognised nothing as of the FY26 10-K (20 July 2026), while CBP's CAPE refund channel has been paying out on a 60-90 day cycle since 20 April 2026 and a direct import peer, RH, recognised $55.1m of IEEPA refunds in the quarter ended 1 August 2026 - four weeks BEFORE MillerKnoll's quarter closed on 29 August.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: MillerKnoll has no prior refund print. The nearest analogue is a below-operating-income item: the $92.3m of goodwill impairments taken in Q3 FY25, whose print (sealed baseline, event_date 2025-03-26) moved +10.69% - the market looked straight through the non-operating charge. That says items below the line neither help nor hurt this name much on their own, which is why this is [sizing note removed]. There is no stated path from a refund to the FY27 guide, so I file it as one_off and not as guidance.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 10-K itself says 'the amount and timing of any refunds that may be realized remain uncertain', so no sell-side model can carry it - the Investing.com preview published this morning frames the quarter as a cost-inflation margin test and never mentions a refund, and the consensus EPS of $0.35 has not moved in 60 days. If the market had priced a refund, a name whose forward PE is 10.0 would not be down 10.9% over the month against -1.7% for its peer group, and the estimate line would have drifted up after RH's 10 September disclosure. Amount is unquantified by the company: MillerKnoll's disclosed NET tariff impacts were ~$7.0m (Q4 FY25), ~$8.0m (Q1 FY26) and ~$1.0m (Q2 FY26), which are after pricing offsets, so gross IEEPA duties eligible for recovery are larger than those figures but I will not invent the number - the band reflects that.
evidence.independence: RH's 10 September 2026 shareholder letter is the independent second source and it is a different company and a different filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001528849/000110465926106743/rh-20260910xex99d2.htm ($55.1m recognised in Q2, $13.9m more expected in H2). Third, CBP's own refund mechanics: https://www.ghy.com/trade-compliance/cbp-cape-ieepa-refund-progress/ (CAPE Phase 1 open 2026-04-20, refunds generally issued 60-90 days after acceptance, ~$128.68bn accepted for processing as of August 2026). This finding shares the FY26 10-K with the goodwill finding below; that is flagged there too.

evidence.text: The only demand evidence dated after MillerKnoll last guided (2026-06-24) is positive and comes from the largest direct competitor's primary release: HNI's 30 July 2026 Q2 exhibit states Workplace Furnishings orders +5% organic, that 'over the most recent five-week period, the year-over-year segment order growth rate accelerated', and guides segment volume growth positive in Q3 with high-single-digit organic growth in H2 - a period that sits inside MillerKnoll's fiscal Q1 (1 June - 29 August 2026), against a Q1 FY26 comparison of consolidated orders -5.4% and North America Contract orders -8.2%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders alone have NOT paid on this name and I have sized for that: on 2026-03-25 North America Contract orders printed +13.1% reported and the stock fell 22.37% on a $0.02 EPS miss; on 2026-06-24 orders printed -6.3% with backlog -10.8% and the stock rose 12.01% on an EPS beat at the top of guidance. So the order line is only worth anything here through the FY27 guide ($3.93-4.13bn, ~5% growth), which is why I file this under guidance rather than reported_quarter: what an accelerating industry order rate buys is that the guide survives contact with an entering backlog down 10.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: MillerKnoll is covered by three analysts (two Buy at a $35 mean target, StoneX at Hold) and the consensus EPS has been flat for 60 days, so nothing in the estimate record shows the HNI read-through being taken. If it had been, the stock would not have de-rated 10.9% over the month while the business-services peer group fell 1.7%, and the pre-print article on the wire this morning would not be framing the quarter as a cost-inflation margin test with no mention of order momentum. HNI is also a different shareholder base - a multi-billion-dollar industrial - and MillerKnoll's own last-reported order line (-10.0% North America) is the number the tape is anchored on.
evidence.independence: Second, unrelated source: StoneX's August 2026 Commercial Dealer Survey, reported as showing 'continued resilience of demand and optimism for future demand' (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/millerknoll-earnings-in-focus-as-new-ceo-faces-margin-test-93CH-4909208, 2026-09-21) - the dealer channel both companies sell through, and notably it comes from the one analyst on this name who is NOT a Buy. Net of the rest of the company: this evidence covers North America Contract plus International Contract, roughly 70% of revenue. The other ~30% is Global Retail, where the direct read-through is RH calling this 'the worst housing market in four decades' while still printing +2.6% revenue and guiding FY26 to +5.5-7.0% - low growth, not a collapse, consistent with MillerKnoll's own Global Retail orders +2.0% organic last quarter. I have trimmed the size for that 30% rather than sizing on the contract read alone. Cuts the other way at a longer horizon: the AIA/Deltek ABI was 47.2 in August with an 18th consecutive monthly decline in design contracts (https://archinect.com/news/article/150500752/architecture-billings-index-reports-continued-soft-business-conditions-in-august) - that leads contract furniture by 9-12 months, so it bears on FY28 and is in every furniture preview already; I dropped it as a separate finding rather than double-count the same demand line in two directions.

evidence.text: The FY26 10-K discloses that the Global Retail reporting unit's fair value exceeded carrying value by just 1.1%, International Contract by 3.1%, and the Muuto and Knoll indefinite-lived trade names by 2.1% and 6.8% - cushions thin enough that the company says 'relatively modest adverse changes' in projected revenue growth or margin would produce material impairment charges, and MillerKnoll has form for taking interim impairments mid-year when performance disappoints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The direct precedent is MillerKnoll's own: in Q3 FY25 management identified interim triggering events and took $30.1m (Global Retail) and $62.2m (Holly Hunt) of non-cash goodwill impairment, and that print (sealed baseline, event_date 2025-03-26) moved +10.69%. The market looked straight through a $92m charge. That history is the whole reason this is [sizing note removed].4 and not at -2: the charge itself is not what this stock pays for, and it only matters as a signal that management has cut the Global Retail plan, which would show up in the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: A 1.1% cushion is a critical-audit-matter footnote in a long 10-K filed in July on a three-analyst name; no aggregator carries reporting-unit cushion percentages and no preview mentions it. If it were priced, the forward PE would not be 10.0 with two of three analysts at a $35 target - a 69% upside target is not what a book carrying a near-zero goodwill cushion on 30% of revenue looks like.
evidence.independence: None that is genuinely independent. This rests on the SAME document as the IEEPA finding above (the FY26 10-K) and I say so here rather than let the sum treat them as two corroborating reads - they are two different disclosures in one filing, and only the refund one has an outside corroborator. The honest weakness, which is why the number is small: the impairment is a hypothesis about what management will decide this quarter, not a fact about the print, and the one time it happened the stock went up.

evidence.text: KB Home goes into this print with average community count up roughly 8% YoY (Q3-2025 average 259 / ending 264; Q2-2026 average 278 up 9%, Q3-2026 ending guided 270-280) and a cancellation rate of 12% of gross orders against 17% in the year-ago Q3 - so its net-order line has two mechanical tailwinds that Lennar, whose -9% order print is what the market marked KBH down on, does not have.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net orders is the one line in the release that is not guided, so it is where a genuine surprise can sit. On 2026-06-23 KBH printed net orders of 3,317 (-4% YoY) against a sector reading far worse and rose 16.65% the next session despite missing EPS $0.43 vs $0.45; on 2025-09-24 net orders of 2,950 (-4%) landed in line and the stock moved -0.63%. The line pays when it separates KBH from the sector read and is ignored when it tracks it.
evidence.why_not_priced: KBH fell 12.6% over 20 sessions and roughly tracked Lennar's post-print de-rating. If the market had done this arithmetic it would not have applied Lennar's -9% pace decline one-for-one to a company carrying ~8% more selling communities and 5 percentage points fewer cancellations: at Q3-2025's 3.8 monthly absorption per community KBH needs only 3.4 (a -11% pace decline, worse than Lennar's) on 280 communities to print net orders down just 3% YoY. Every published preview frames tonight as 'will orders hold' in the abstract and none of them carries the community base. Net of the rest of the company: deliveries and margin are both inside the company's own June guide and therefore cannot surprise much either way, so this line is not being offset by a hidden negative elsewhere in the release - the offset is the forward guide, which I size separately and negatively below.
evidence.independence: The community-count and cancellation figures come from two DIFFERENT KB Home releases (Q3-2025 8-K of 2025-09-24 above and the Q2-2026 8-K of 2026-06-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/795266/000079526626000060/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm), so this is not one document read twice. Pointing the same way from an unrelated source: Hovnanian, reporting the quarter ended 31 July 2026, said sales pace stayed 'resilient, with contracts per community above historical averages' while total contracts fell - i.e. the sector's order decline is a community/pace composition effect, which is the variable KBH is long of (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/20/3348449/12793/en/hovnanian-enterprises-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results.html).

evidence.text: The Q3 delivery guide of 2,600-2,800 homes implies only 57-62% conversion of the 4,526-home backlog KBH carried into the quarter, against 66.5% actually converted in Q2-2026 (2,395 delivered from an opening backlog of 3,604) and ~71% in Q3-2025 (3,393 from ~4,764) - so the revenue guide carries a conversion cushion.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deliveries landing inside the guided range has not moved this stock in either direction: 2025-09-24 deliveries 3,393 (in range), move -0.63%; 2026-03-24 deliveries 2,370, move -1.55%. The two large moves in the baseline (+16.65%, -8.54%) both came off the forward guide, not the delivery line.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is arithmetic off two primary documents that no aggregator publishes - the opening backlog is derived (4,526 ending + 2,395 delivered - 3,317 net orders = 3,604 opening), and the conversion series is not in any preview. But I size it small and say why: this outcome lands INSIDE what the company guided on 23 June, so the market has already been told to expect it, and the conversion rate legitimately falls as the built-to-order mix lengthens cycle times. The honest read is that it lowers the probability of a delivery MISS rather than creating a beat, and the +0.5 reflects exactly that and nothing more.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q2-2026 8-K with finding 1 - counted once between them, which is why this one is [sizing note removed].5 rather than at the standalone value of a conversion cushion. The 71% Q3-2025 comparator comes from a different document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/795266/000079526625000092/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm).

evidence.text: Two peer builders printed sequential gross-margin IMPROVEMENT in windows that overlap KBH's June-August quarter and that both landed after KBH last spoke on 23 June: Lennar's Q3 (identical 31 August quarter end) went 15.3% to 15.8% with incentives moderating to 12%, and Hovnanian's quarter ended 31 July was its SECOND consecutive sequential gross-margin improvement - which is the same shape as KBH's guided step from 15.2% to 16.0-16.6%.

evidence.text: The obvious bear read of the H2-to-date pace comment — index VIX at its 2026 low, therefore a repeat of the H2 2025 collapse that got the last September print sold — is probably keyed to the wrong market parameter: the company states the Jan-May surge happened in conditions 'broadly comparable' to the prior year, making it capability rather than weather, and H2 2026 has carried record single-stock dispersion with S&P 500 pairwise correlation in the bottom 1% since 2005.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the decisive line on this name in September. On 2025-09-23 the reported half was outstanding — net income doubled, ROE 20.3%, two EUR0.10 interims declared — and the stock fell 1.51%, because the release flagged that volatility had returned to historically low levels since June and H2 activity was down on H1. Kepler's later summary of that year confirms the mechanism: 'l'annee a ete marquee par un premier semestre tres solide, suivi de conditions de marche moins favorables au second semestre'. Conversely on 2026-03-24 a +40% pace statement was NOT enough to save a print whose P&L missed. So a constructive pace comment is necessary but not sufficient, and a weak one is close to sufficient for a negative day.
evidence.why_not_priced: The visible, quotable, terminal-level statistic on volatility is the VIX, and it is at its 2026 low — 14.2 on 2026-08-14 and 14.81 at the close on 2026-09-18, down from 21.51 in early June. Anyone previewing this print off the wire copy reaches for that number and reproduces the September-2025 trade. What the VIX does not describe is the environment a relative-value arbitrageur is actually paid in: on 2026-07-09 the Cboe S&P 500 Constituent Volatility Index closed at 49.98 against a VIX of 15.84, an all-time record 34.14-point gap and the 98th percentile for VIXEQ, and as of 2026-08-14 the average 60-day pairwise correlation among S&P 500 constituents sat in the bottom 1% of observations since 2005. Low index vol produced by low correlation and high single-stock vol is the opposite regime, for this business, from the genuinely quiet summer of 2025. If the market had made this distinction the stock would not be flat-to-down through a quarter in which its own disclosed activity pace accelerated from +40% (20 March) to +70% (end May). I am sizing this at less than half of finding 1 because LESSONS.md is explicit that macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and no [THE COMPANY] document names dispersion; the company statement I quote covers January-May, not July-September.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution is the single most reliably price-moving line on this name, and it has cut both ways.
